story.conflict: A bride must decide whether protecting her husband's business justifies letting him sell a choice that belongs to her.
story.hook: My groom sold our first dance to a client without asking me. When I refused, he said his business depended on keeping that man happy.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF THE DANCE WAS HER CHOICE
story.premise: A groom sells his first dance with the bride to a business client without asking her, then says his business depends on her honoring the deal.
story.punchline: That night, I danced to it with my mum.
story.script: Daniel waved the man over and told me to get ready for our song. The client thanked me for agreeing. I said I hadn't. Daniel laughed and said I was being shy. I asked him how much he'd taken. Five thousand dollars, he said, and it had helped pay for the wedding. The client stopped smiling. He'd been told this was something we'd offered together. Daniel said the man could take his business elsewhere if I embarrassed him. I asked why he'd made that my responsibility. He said it was only a dance. I said if it meant so little, he could explain that when he gave the money back. He admitted he'd already spent it. Then he asked whether I'd really let one song spoil the whole evening. I went back to the client and said I hadn't agreed to the arrangement. He said he wasn't going to dance with someone who didn't want to. Daniel asked me to smile so the guests wouldn't notice. I told him I wasn't pretending we'd made this decision together. When the song started, my mum asked whether I wanted to sit outside or dance with her. I took her hand. Daniel was still trying to catch my eye. He kept calling it our song. That night, I danced to it with my mum.
story.twist: The client believed the bride had agreed, and the groom's claim that the dance is harmless becomes harder to defend when he admits he has already spent the money.

youtube.description: The client thinks the bride agreed to the arrangement. Her groom has already accepted the money.
youtube.title: The Client Waiting for Their First Dance

story.conflict: A husband must face that frightening his wife into staying is control rather than evidence that she cares about him.
story.hook: I paid a stranger to pretend to attack me. I wanted my wife to cancel her first work trip.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF FEAR IS NOT SUPPORT
story.premise: A husband pays a stranger to stage an attack on him so his wife will cancel her first work trip to stay home and care for him.
story.punchline: This time, I couldn't call that the emergency.
story.script: Nina pushed her suitcase against the wall and called her boss. She kept apologizing for letting the team down. I'd told her I was afraid to be alone. Then the man I'd hired came back to collect the rest of his money. I tried to send him away. He looked at her, then asked whether she really thought I'd been attacked. I told him to leave. He said he wasn't going to stand there while she blamed herself for planning to go. Nina asked me what I'd paid him to do. I admitted the attack had been staged. She asked whether I'd let her cancel the trip knowing that. I said I'd been afraid she'd start choosing work over me. She said she'd asked me about the trip weeks ago, and I'd told her I was proud of her. I said I hadn't known how to tell her I wanted her home. She pointed at her suitcase and asked why frightening her had seemed easier. I tried to say it hadn't meant anything would happen to her. She said I'd made her believe something had happened to me. She called her boss back and said she could travel after all. Then she said she wasn't ready to discuss what happened when she returned. The suitcase was by the door again. This time, I couldn't call that the emergency.
story.twist: The man hired to play the attacker sees the wife's distress and refuses to keep helping conceal the scheme.

youtube.description: He says he is proud of his wife's opportunity. Then he pays someone to give her a reason to stay home.
youtube.title: The Suitcase He Wanted Unpacked

story.conflict: An employee must defend his reputation when his boss treats a believable performance as permission to present him as a real thief.
story.hook: I found a video calling me a thief playing above my own checkout. My boss had staged the theft himself for staff training.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF ACTING IS NOT A CONFESSION
story.premise: A shop owner presents an employee's staged theft-training performance as a real crime in a customer-facing security-camera advertisement.
story.punchline: For once, the video upsetting him showed what I'd actually done.
story.script: A customer asked another employee to serve her because she'd seen what I did. Above us, I was taking cash from a drawer. We'd filmed it after closing, with Leo telling me to make it look believable. The display now said our cameras had caught a thief. I asked him to take it down. He said customers knew those videos were demonstrations. I pointed to the woman refusing my help. He said calling it staged would make the cameras harder to sell. He told me to stop discussing it in front of customers. I opened the full clip. It began with Leo handing me the notes and telling me when to start. He said I was making him look dishonest. I asked why my reputation was the part we could spend. He offered to film me saying customers had misunderstood. I offered the truth. He started recording. I said we'd staged the theft together, and he'd removed the explanation before putting it on display. He stopped recording and told me to leave that part out. I recorded my own explanation and posted it. Leo said we'd discuss my future at the shop. For once, the video upsetting him showed what I'd actually done.
story.twist: The boss wants the employee to call the accusation a misunderstanding while keeping the sales benefit of an advertisement he deliberately made misleading.

youtube.description: Customers recognize the employee from a theft video. His boss knows exactly how that scene was made.
youtube.title: The Training Clip Above His Checkout

story.conflict: A patient must protect her own body when a dentist presents an unsafe demand as a reasonable return policy.
story.hook: My dentist offered a refund if I pulled out the veneers myself. When I refused, he said I was choosing to keep what I'd paid for.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF THAT REFUND HAD STRINGS
story.premise: A dentist makes a refund conditional on the patient pulling out and returning the veneers he fitted, then calls her dishonest when she refuses.
story.punchline: He wasn't getting to decide what I did to my mouth as well.
story.script: I'd gone back because the veneers weren't the shade we'd agreed. He said I could return them like anything else. I asked him to arrange that safely. He said removal wasn't included in a refund, and I could bring them back loose. I said I wasn't taking anything off my teeth myself. He called that wanting the work for free. I asked how refusing to hurt myself meant I was happy with what he'd done. No return, no refund, he said. At the reception desk, he told me I was refusing a solution. A woman waiting nearby asked what solution he meant. He said I wanted my money back while keeping the veneers. I said he'd told me to remove them myself. He told me not to alarm other patients. The woman asked whether he'd expect that of her, too. He said every case was different. She picked up her bag and said she wasn't going ahead with her appointment. He turned back to me and said we could discuss options if I calmed down. I asked whether any option involved him taking responsibility for the work. He said he'd call me. I left without a refund and arranged another opinion. He still had my money. He wasn't getting to decide what I did to my mouth as well.
story.twist: The dentist calls keeping the attached veneers dishonest, but retreats from explaining the same demand when a waiting patient hears it.

youtube.description: The patient asks the dentist to correct his work. He insists the veneers must be returned before discussing a refund.
youtube.title: The Veneers He Wanted Back Loose
